candidates.title: DRLLMS: Network-Adaptive Reasoning Control for Interactive LLM Streaming
candidates.venue: International Workshop on Network and Operating System Support for Digital Audio and Video
candidates.abstract: In interactive LLM streaming, lengthy chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning delays the delivery of user-consumable content, degrading responsiveness, particularly under variable network conditions. Existing methods, however, fail to adapt CoT length to network dynamics. We propose DRLLMS, a network-adaptive framework that treats CoT length as a control knob to optimize Quality of Experience (QoE). Our analysis, centered on a new metric, Time-to-First-Answer (TTFA), confirms that this pre-answer reasoning is the primary latency bottleneck. DRLLMS employs a reinforcement learning strategy to enable controllable CoT generation and, at runtime, uses a lightweight optimizer to select the optimal CoT length based on network conditions. Experiments demonstrate that DRLLMS effectively balances responsiveness and answer quality, improving user experience across diverse bandwidth scenarios.
candidates.reason: 要旨では対話型LLMストリーミングでネットワーク状況に応じてChain-of-Thought長を強化学習と軽量最適化で制御し、Time-to-First-Answerを主指標にQoEを改善するDRLLMSを提案しており、LLMサービング／ストリーミング配信の直接的な最適化として確認できる。

candidates.title: Lossless Token Sequence Compression via Meta-Tokens
candidates.abstract: Existing work on prompt compression for Large Language Models (LLM) focuses on lossy methods that try to maximize the retention of semantic information that is relevant to downstream tasks while significantly reducing the sequence length. In this paper, we introduce a task-agnostic lossless compression technique similar to LZ77 that makes it possible to reduce the input token sequence length on average by 27\% and 18\% for the two evaluation tasks explored here. Given that we use transformer-based LLMs, this equates to 47\% and 33\% less encoding computation, respectively, due to the quadratic nature of attention. The token sequence transformation is trivial to reverse and highlights that no semantic information is lost in the process. We evaluate our proposed approach on two tasks that require strict preservation of semantics/syntax and demonstrate that existing lossy compression methods perform poorly in this setting. We find that our lossless compression technique produces only a small gap in performance compared to using the uncompressed input and posit that larger models and an expanded computing budget would likely erase the gap entirely.
candidates.reason: arXiv要旨ではLZ77類似の可逆なメタトークン化で入力トークン列を平均27%圧縮し、注意の二次計算によりエンコーディング計算を47%削減する無損失プロンプト圧縮を提案しており、LLM推論の前処理計算を直接削減する手法として確認できる。

candidates.title: DEQ: Dynamic Element-wise Quantization for Efficient Attention Architecture
candidates.abstract: Attention-based models, such as transformers, have achieved remarkable success across various tasks. However, their deployment is hindered by challenges such as high memory requirements, long inference latency, and significant power consumption. Quantization has emerged as an effective approach to address these challenges by reducing the bit-width of the model. However, existing quantization algorithms suffer from too coarse-grained quantization granularity or statically determining the bit-width of tokens, lacking the flexibility needed to achieve maximum performance improvement. Accordingly, in this paper, we present a Dynamic Element-wise Quantization (DEQ) algorithm that dynamically tunes tokens’ bit-width according to the importance of elements in the attention possibilities matrix.On the hardware side, we design three versions of DEQ architectures to progressively improve the performance of the DEQ algorithm. The proposed DEQ architecture can address the under-utilization and workload imbalance problems by 1) supporting multiple precision computations on a single systolic array for generality, 2) decoupling the rows in the systolic array for enough flexibility, 3) identifying and parallelizing the independent computations within one systolic array for high parallelism. Extensive experiment results demonstrate that DEQ can achieve satisfactory performance speedups and energy saving compared to state-of-the-art designs.
candidates.reason: 要旨では注意確率行列の要素重要度に応じてトークンのビット幅を動的に変えるDEQ量子化と、それを支える複数精度systolic array等のハードウェアアーキテクチャを提案し、Transformer推論の速度とエネルギーを改善しており直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Grasp: Group-based Prediction of Activation Sparsity for Fast LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: Optimizing LLM inference has become increasingly important as the demand for efficient on-device deployments grows. To reduce the computational overhead in the MLP components, which account for a significant portion of LLM inference, ReLU-fied LLMs have been introduced to maximize activation sparsity. Several sparsity prediction methods have been developed to efficiently skip unnecessary memory accesses and computations by predicting activation sparsity. In this paper, we propose a novel magnitude-based, training-free sparsity prediction technique called Grasp that builds on the existing sign bitbased method for ReLU-fied LLMs. The proposed method enhances prediction accuracy by grouping values considering the distribution within vectors and explicitly accounting for statistical outliers. This allows us to estimate the impact of each element more accurately yet in an efficient way, improving both activation sparsity prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Compared to the-state-of-the-art technique, Grasp achieves higher sparsity prediction accuracy and $11 \%$ higher skipping efficiency, which corresponds to $1.85 \times$ speedup against the dense inference.
candidates.reason: 要旨ではReLU化LLMのMLPにおける活性化スパース性をグループ単位で予測するGraspを提案し、不要なメモリアクセスと計算をスキップして密な推論比1.85倍の高速化を示しており、LLM推論の直接的な高速化手法として確認できる。
